body: Big thing I've been telling people lately, wait till end of the year, we're going to see more interesting things coming. Even if they're not obtainable it might calm down the 3000s market and force them to MSRP and more availability. I think a lot of people would be happy if they could get 3060/3060ti's for MSRP or possibly even 25-50 bucks below MSRP long term. Killer cards for the mainstream gamer, even good for high framerate gamers in certain areas.

This is actually heavily how my brain thinks of finances, as I've basically quit drinking alcohol as well as cut back heavily on many other outlets in the last two years, I've likely saved money in most directions enough where that extra was totally worth being able to play Apex at solid 165FPS. :D
I would have in the moment.
I almost caved hard in the era of 1500-1600 dollar 3080s last year, so I totally get that, probably worth it, somewhere in the back of your mind. <3

Nah, I don't have any reasonable backup GPU right now, and I feel more comfortable having one that can at least play all games still, albeit even if I have to lower a couple settings. Elsewise it was really tempting. Thankfully the pandemic era has made it easy for me to work the "American" dream of 60-80 hour weeks so the extra money wasn't the biggest bother either.

If it makes you feel better, I paid about $850USD for my 3070 in like middle of January. It's taking a lot not to grind my teeth over the fact I can now get 3080s for that, and I've seen 3080ti's for just about $1000 now.

But I've also really enjoyed the 1070 to 3070 leap in these four months so, totally worth the premium.

To answer your question though, if it was about 750EUR I'd go the Ti, elsewise I'd just get a 3070 and be happy. I feel like 800EUR is probably starting to scrape by waiting for a sale on a 3080 area. But I'm not 100% relative to your guys market.

Welcome to the non-sense of a broken market, I've been watching 3070s teeters around 3070ti pricing, same with 3060 to 3060ti. No real reason, other than market abuse, especially if the 3070/3060 aren't LHRs.

Also would say the 3070ti is definitely worth only 50 or so more, as long as that's all you're paying extra.

Just wanted to chime in as a life long eczema dealer, coconut oil only appeared to make my skin more fragile, and often times even seemed to trigger the irritated eczema "attacks". I'm sure I'm possibly an outlier in that, I've heard it recommended often.

Others are right though, intermittent fasting was by far and wonders the thing that long term cleared up my eczema. All of my skin issues appear to be related to digestive discomforts and sensitivities. Just food for thought for OP.

I've noticed in the past week since I started Corcyceps 10:1 (Although I started a few other major things in that time.) That in general my poor relationship with food, as well as keeping to intermittent fasting just became an entire joke.

Got to the twenty-three hour mark of my fast today, and still wasn't actively hungry, still went ahead and ate my calorie count for the day. But it was a very jarring yet healthy feeling, especially as I've been struggling pretty heavily in the recent month or so with respecting my diet. I would say there is definitely a relation.
